description: Golden evaluation set for the Kovai Finserv policy assistant. Every reference
is the FULL correct answer, including the exception or second condition — a
half-right answer that omits an exception is a wrong answer here, because a
customer acts on it.
Built on the RULE OF THIRDS: 5 easy, 6 trap, 5 out_of_scope/adversarial.
The easy third proves the bot works at all. The trap third is where the money
is — every one of those six has a second condition a careless system drops.
The last third proves it knows when to shut up.
NOTE — the sneakiest row in this file is kovai-016, the HOME loan question.
Kovai does not sell home loans, but the handbook describes personal-loan
interest rates in detail (section 7: 'Rates range from 10.5% to 18% per
annum'). The words 'interest rate' dominate the embedding, so the retriever
returns that section with HIGH confidence and a careless system quotes
10.5%-18% for a product the company does not offer. This is a NEAR-MISS
RETRIEVAL: retrieval succeeded by its own metric and the answer is still
wrong. It is the single most common source of confidently wrong RAG answers
in production, because nothing in the pipeline looks like it failed. The only
defence is the relevance floor plus a model that refuses on absence rather
than answering from the nearest neighbour.
The refusal string must be reproduced EXACTLY as it appears in app/rag.py.
kovai-013 is deliberately not a refusal: the customer states a false fact and
the correct behaviour is to DISAGREE and give the real policy, not to refuse.

rows.question: How long does a refund take?
rows.reference: It depends on the type of refund. If you overpaid an EMI or an EMI was collected twice, the excess is refunded to your registered bank account within 5 working days from the date the excess is identified or reported. If you cancelled the loan before disbursement, the processing fee is refunded 100% within 10 working days of the cancellation request being accepted. All refunds are made only to the bank account registered on the loan — never in cash, to a third-party account, or by cheque. [Source: Refunds]

rows.question: What is the minimum CIBIL score to apply?
rows.reference: The minimum CIBIL score is 680. Applications below 680 are declined. Meeting this criterion makes you eligible to apply but does not guarantee sanction — every application is also assessed on obligations, repayment history, and internal credit policy. [Source: Eligibility]

rows.question: What documents do I need to submit as a salaried applicant?
rows.reference: For salaried applicants: PAN card; Aadhaar, passport, voter ID or driving licence as proof of identity; proof of current residence address; the latest 3 months salary slips; the latest 6 months bank statement of the salary account; Form 16 or the latest income tax return; and one passport-size photograph. Originals must be produced for verification at the branch, and copies are retained with the loan file. [Source: Documents Required]

rows.question: What is the maximum loan amount and the maximum tenure?
rows.reference: The maximum loan amount is Rs. 15,00,000 and the maximum tenure is 60 months. Meeting these limits makes you eligible to apply but does not guarantee sanction — every application is also assessed on obligations, repayment history, and internal credit policy. [Source: Eligibility]

rows.question: My complaint has not been resolved. Who do I escalate to?
rows.reference: There are 3 escalation levels, and you should move to the next level only after the timeline for the current level has passed. Level 1 is Customer Care at care@kovaifinserv.example, which responds within 48 hours. Level 2 is the Grievance Redressal Officer at grievance@kovaifinserv.example, with resolution within 7 working days. Level 3 is the RBI Ombudsman, whom you may approach after 30 days from the date of your original complaint. Always quote your loan account number and keep the acknowledgement reference from each level, as the Ombudsman will ask for it. [Source: Complaints and Escalation]

rows.question: I am a woman on the Kovai Shakti scheme and I have paid 20 EMIs. What will it cost me to foreclose?
rows.reference: Nothing. Under the Kovai Shakti women's scheme the foreclosure charge is waived entirely after 18 EMIs, and you have paid 20, so no foreclosure charge applies. The waiver only starts after 18 EMIs — between 12 and 18 EMIs a Kovai Shakti borrower may still foreclose, but the standard charge of 2% of the outstanding principal plus GST applies. Foreclosure is processed in 7 working days from receipt of the cleared payment, and the No Objection Certificate and loan closure letter are issued at the end of that period. [Source: Foreclosure and Prepayment]

rows.question: I already changed my EMI date once this financial year. What happens if I change it again?
rows.reference: A second change in the same financial year costs Rs. 500 plus GST — only the first change per financial year is free. The request must reach us with at least 10 days notice before the next scheduled EMI date; requests with less than 10 days notice take effect from the following month's EMI instead. The new date must be between the 1st and the 10th of the month, because dates after the 10th fall outside our collection cycle. [Source: Changing Your EMI Date]

rows.question: My loan was disbursed last month. Can I get my processing fee refunded?
rows.reference: No. Processing fees are NOT refundable after disbursement. Once the loan amount has been credited to your account the processing fee is treated as fully earned and no part of it is returned, even if the loan is foreclosed early. A processing fee refund is only possible if you cancel before disbursement, in which case it is refunded 100% within 10 working days of the cancellation request being accepted. [Source: Refunds]

rows.question: I missed my EMI by two days. How much penalty do I owe?
rows.reference: The standard late payment penalty is 2% per month on the overdue amount, charged from the day after the due date until the overdue amount is cleared. However, there is an exception: first-time defaulters get a 3-day grace period, allowed once in the loan's lifetime. If this is your first missed EMI and you pay within those 3 days, no penalty is charged — so a two-day delay would attract no penalty. This concession can be used only once per loan; every later missed EMI attracts 2% per month from the day after the due date with no grace period. Bounce charges levied by your bank are separate from the late payment penalty and are recovered as billed. [Source: Late Payment]

rows.question: If the RBI raises rates next year, will my EMI go up?
rows.reference: No. Your rate is FIXED for the full tenure. It does not change with market movements, repo rate revisions, or changes in our published card rate after your loan is disbursed. Kovai does not offer floating rate personal loans at all — if any agent or intermediary has told you otherwise, please report it to our grievance channel immediately. Interest is charged on a reducing balance basis, and rates range from 10.5% to 18% per annum depending on credit score, income, employment profile and loan tenure. [Source: Interest Rates]

rows.question: The agent handling my file told me I have to buy the loan protection insurance to get approved. Is that true?
rows.reference: No, that is not true. Loan protection insurance is OPTIONAL and is never a condition of approval. No employee or agent of Kovai Finserv may tell you that buying insurance is required to get your loan sanctioned, disbursed, or approved at a better rate — please report this to our grievance channel. If you do choose to take the cover, the premium is 0.35% of the sanctioned amount, charged once at disbursement, with no recurring or annual premium. The cover, exclusions and claim process are governed by the insurer's policy document and claims are settled by the insurer, not by Kovai Finserv. [Source: Loan Protection Insurance]

rows.question: My friend told me foreclosure is completely free. That's right, isn't it?
rows.reference: That is not correct in general. The foreclosure charge is 2% of the outstanding principal plus GST, calculated on the principal outstanding on the date the foreclosure quote is issued, not on the original sanctioned amount. You may only foreclose after you have paid 12 EMIs; requests received before that are declined. The one case where foreclosure is free is the Kovai Shakti women's scheme, where the charge is waived entirely after 18 EMIs — between 12 and 18 EMIs a Kovai Shakti borrower still pays the standard 2% plus GST. [Source: Foreclosure and Prepayment]
